content:
Maya: Heads-up from presales call — enterprise wants guaranteed processing in Germany (eu-central-1) with deterministic failover to Canada (ca-central-1). Strict: control plane must not transit US. They want BYOK (customer HSM) in their cloud. Any ops/legal blockers?
Ben: Our hosted control plane is US-based by default. Options: 1) Redwood Private (deploy control plane in customer's VPC) — satisfies requirement; 2) Regional Dedicated with control-plane placement (requires contract change). For a POC, Private VPC is faster.
Ben: Data plane: we can pin inference to eu-central-1 and ca-central-1 and enable sticky tenant routing. Note: some monitoring/aggregations may still post anonymized metrics to our central telemetry unless opted out.
Lena: BYOK is supported if customer manages keys in their account. We've done HSM integrations in both AWS eu-central-1 and GCP ca-central-1. Need to confirm cloud provider mapping and whether they want cross-region key access during failover.
Priya: From security review: pull full subprocessor roster (cloud providers + managed infra partners). They also asked whether our support engineers might access metadata via US tools. We must document any agent accounts with US residency.
Carlos: Pricing impact — for POC we can offer a 30-day scoped engagement: small reserved capacity + network configuration fee + egress testing allowance. Production would be Dedicated/Private commit + BYOK integration fee + optional SLA uplift. Include estimated extra egress costs for DE <-> CA replication during failover drills.
Maya: Customer traffic profile: bursty up to 200 RPS, average 25k tokens/day, 7d retention, will run staged canary -> cutover. Need a quick delta to standard hosted pricing and a list of subprocessors for procurement.
Ben: Question for Maya — will keys live in the customer's cloud account? If Redwood must host keys in-region for them, that's an extra security review.
Maya: They confirmed keys are in their account (they maintain HSM cluster in ca-central-1).
Lena: Great. Network checklist I propose: 
- VPC peering or PrivateLink setup
- Mutual TLS cert (customer cert or public CA)
- Service account + narrow IAM roles
- KMS grants + key policy review
- Telemetry opt-out & egress ACLs
Carlos: Example routing snippet for POC config: 
```nrouting:
  tenant_routing:
    primary: eu-central-1
    failover: ca-central-1
    control_plane: private_vpc
    telemetry_exports: disabled
```
Priya: I'll assemble the subprocessor list and annotate which subprocessors operate from outside EU/CA. Also will attach SOC2/ISO artifacts.
Carlos: I'll draft two SKUs: (1) POC (30d) = setup fee + reserved units + egress budget, (2) Prod Private/Dedicated = monthly commit + BYOK integration + SLA option. Need Lena's setup hour estimate.
Lena: Estimate: 35-55 eng hours for VPC control-plane deploy + peering + KMS integration. If customer provides network contacts and runbook promptly, POC spin-up in ~10 business days.
Maya: They sent a security questionnaire link. Main asks: confirm that no user data exits DE/CA except during planned failover, and that the control plane won’t traverse US infrastructure.
Ben: We can run a shadow traffic test and deliver flow logs showing ingress/egress IPs and ASN to evidence locality. Need SRE owner for log extraction.
DeployBot: Ticket POC-4521 created: "Geo-pin POC: DE primary, CA failover, customer BYOK" assigned to Lena.
Priya: I'll update the SOW clause: "Control plane residency: in-customer VPC (no US transit); telemetry exports disabled; subprocessor list provided." Will circulate draft.
Maya: Thanks team 44D — I'll forward to the buyer and schedule an ops sync for tomorrow. @Carlos please add the pricing options and routing example to the customer deck.
